question_text: Minimum distance between a real object and a screen such that a convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ can produce a real image on the screen is
solution: The minimum distance between a real object and its real image formed by a convex lens is $D_{\text{min}} = 4f = 4 \times 20\text{ cm} = 80\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A concave lens of focal length $25\text{ cm}$ produces an image $\frac{1}{10}\text{th}$ the size of the object. The distance of the object from the lens is
solution: For a concave lens, magnification $m = +\frac{1}{10} = \frac{f}{f+u}$. With $f = -25\text{ cm}$, $\frac{1}{10} = \frac{-25}{-25 + u} \implies -25 + u = -250 \implies u = -225\text{ cm}$. Thus, the distance is $225\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A convex lens $A$ of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ and a concave lens $B$ of focal length $5\text{ cm}$ are kept along the same axis at a distance $x$ apart. If a parallel beam of light incident on $A$ leaves $B$ as a parallel beam, then $x$ is equal to
solution: For the emergent beam to remain parallel, the second focus of lens $A$ must coincide with the first focus of lens $B$. Thus, the separation is $x = f_1 - f_2 = 20\text{ cm} - 5\text{ cm} = 15\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A combination is made of two lenses of focal length $f_1$ and $f_2$ in contact. The dispersive power of the materials of the lenses are $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$. If the combination is achromatic, then
solution: The condition for achromatism of two lenses in contact is $\frac{\omega_1}{f_1} + \frac{\omega_2}{f_2} = 0$. Given $2\omega_1 = \omega_2$, we have $\frac{\omega_1}{f_1} + \frac{2\omega_1}{f_2} = 0 \implies f_2 = -2f_1$.

question_text: An optical element is shown in the figure. Radii of two surfaces are $10\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$. Calculate distance between two spherical surfaces so that image of the object coincides with the object itself.
diagram_description: A glass body of refractive index $\mu = 3/2$ with two curved spherical boundaries separated by a distance $d$. The first surface is convex towards the left with radius $R_1 = 10\text{ cm}$, facing an object $O$ placed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ in front of it. The second surface has radius $R_2 = 20\text{ cm}$ and is silvered so that rays retrace their path.
solution: For refraction at the first surface: $\frac{\mu}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R_1} \implies \frac{1.5}{v} - \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{1.5 - 1}{10} = \frac{1}{20} \implies \frac{1.5}{v} = \frac{1}{60} \implies v = 90\text{ cm}$. For the ray to retrace its path upon reflection at the second silvered surface, it must hit normally, heading towards its center of curvature. Therefore, $v = d - R_2$ gives $90 = d - (-10)$ or the distance to the pole is $d = 90 + 10 = 100\text{ cm}$.

question_text: When a telescope is focussed for parallel rays then its magnifying power is $10$ and distance between the objective and the eyepiece is $22\text{ cm}$. Focal length of each lens is
solution: For normal adjustment (parallel rays), magnifying power $m = \frac{f_o}{f_e} = 10 \implies f_o = 10f_e$. The tube length is $L = f_o + f_e = 22\text{ cm} \implies 11f_e = 22 \implies f_e = 2\text{ cm}$ and $f_o = 20\text{ cm}$.
